elements.element: The clause must use one of two permitted renewal mechanisms: renewal only by mutual written agreement, or automatic renewal subject to the requirements below.
elements.evidence: The operative language states that the Agreement “may be renewed only by mutual written agreement of the parties.” Sections II and III likewise require mutual written agreement for extensions.

elements.element: If automatic renewal is used, each automatic renewal term must be 12 months.
elements.evidence: This conditional requirement is inapplicable because the clause demonstrably does not use automatic renewal; renewal is permitted “only by mutual written agreement.”

elements.element: If automatic renewal is used, Customer must be permitted to opt out on 30 days’ notice.
elements.evidence: This conditional requirement is inapplicable because the clause demonstrably does not use automatic renewal.

elements.element: If automatic renewal is used, Vendor must provide a reminder 60 days before renewal.
elements.evidence: This conditional requirement is inapplicable because the clause demonstrably does not use automatic renewal.

elements.element: If automatic renewal is used, renewal price increases must be capped at the lesser of CPI and 3%.
elements.evidence: This conditional requirement is inapplicable because renewal is only by mutual written agreement rather than automatic renewal.
The clause provides for renewal only by mutual written agreement and contains no automatic-renewal mechanism.

elements.element: The automatic-renewal non-renewal notice window must be no more than 60 days.
elements.evidence: No Customer non-renewal right or notice window is stated. The separate 45-day language concerns mutual written extension, not notice to prevent automatic renewal.

elements.element: Renewal price increases must be capped at 5% or less.
elements.evidence: The operative clause contains no express cap on renewal price increases.

result.reason: The redline reaches the preferred mutual-written-agreement pathway by replacing Licensor’s unilateral seven-year renewal option with renewal only by mutual written agreement. Accordingly, the automatic-renewal term, opt-out, reminder, and price-cap requirements are not triggered. The fallback is not satisfied because it specifically requires automatic renewal, a notice window, and a price cap. The change is narrow and leaves unrelated termination and payment provisions intact. Drafting quality is reduced by the retained malformed phrase “mutual written of the parties” and redundant extension provisions, although neither defeats the mutual-written-agreement requirement.
